# 4 Maccabees Chapter 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Remaining Brothers and the Mother

---

**10:1** When the sixth also had died in blessed death, after all his sufferings, the seventh and youngest of all came forward.

**10:2** The tyrant was moved to pity for him — seeing how completely he was surrounded by misfortune — and called him near and urged him to have pity on himself by transgressing the law.

**10:3** But he said: I am the last of my brothers; I will not fall below the rank of my brothers by giving in to your threats, and so I will resist you, as my brothers did before me.

**10:4** What you are doing to me is not murder but cruelty; you are offering me unlawful food in order to get me to abandon God.

**10:5** You cannot compel me by any argument or any forcible means; for I am ruled by a reason that is holy and that makes me worthy of my brothers.

**10:6** For my brothers, having endured a brief pain, have now drunk of ever-flowing life under God's covenant, but you, through the judgment of God, will receive just punishment for your arrogance.

**10:7** I, like my brothers, give up my body and life for the ancestral laws, calling upon God to show mercy quickly to our nation.

**10:8** And I pray that through me and my brothers the wrath of the Almighty that has justly come upon our whole nation may cease.

**10:9** As for me, I give my body and my soul to the hands of God, calling out to him in prayer, O Lord, I am being brought before you and I offer you my blood as a purification — and let this be sufficient for our nation.

**10:10** When he had said this they tortured him even more cruelly than the others, feeling bitter against him because of his scorn.

**10:11** This was in keeping with his noble character, for he too had been educated in the same philosophy and endurance as his brothers.

**10:12** And so, having set his whole soul on God, he died nobly in his torments, as though he were another Eleazar.

**10:13** After the brothers had died, their mother was last of all put to death.

**10:14** It is fitting to praise the mother of the seven beyond any admiration of heroism for she, though beholding the murder of seven children within the space of one day, endured this with good courage because of her hope in God.

**10:15** She exhorted each one of them in the language of their fathers; filled with a noble spirit she fired her feminine reasoning with a manly courage and said to them:

**10:16** I am a pure virgin, and I have not gone out from my father's house; and I did not know this world's pleasures.

**10:17** But I kept myself in chastity and I did not transgress the commandments, nor do I know of sin in me.

**10:18** I will say with my children: God did not give me any other son, and I do not know any other son, for he has taken from me one who should be a memorial of his holy name.

**10:19** So this is my supreme joy: that I gave birth and raised these holy sons and not one of them has been separated from God's purpose.
